name: Saint Angela Merici
history: An Italian laywoman who founded the Company of Saint Ursula, a community of consecrated women who lived in their own homes and served in the world, teaching girls the faith at a time when few girls were taught at all. Her company later grew into the Ursuline nuns, whose schools spread across Europe and the Americas.
life: Angela was born at Desenzano on Lake Garda and lost both parents while still a girl. She became a Franciscan tertiary and gave herself to prayer and to teaching the children of her neighbourhood. Tradition tells of a vision in which she saw a ladder reaching to heaven with young women climbing it, and understood that she was to found a community. She moved to Brescia, where she became known as a peacemaker and counsellor, and made pilgrimages to the Holy Land and to Rome. In 1535, with twenty-eight companions, she founded the Company of Saint Ursula, under the patronage of the virgin martyr. Its members took no vows of enclosure and wore no habit; they lived with their families, prayed and taught girls. After her death the company was reshaped, and in many places it became an enclosed religious order, the Ursulines. She was canonised in 1807.
prayerTo: Saint Angela, you saw that the Church needed women who would teach and serve in the middle of the world. Pray for teachers and all who form the young, for consecrated women, and for me, that I may live my faith at home and at work, and hand it on with patience and love. Amen.
penance: Spend some time today teaching a child something of the faith, a prayer or a story from the Gospel, or give to support a catechist or a Catholic school.
meditation: Angela believed a woman could belong wholly to God without leaving her own home. Where in your daily surroundings is God asking you to belong to Him more completely?
